label: Concepts from Algebra
notes: This appendix covers printed pages 601 through 606 and gathers the abstract algebra used throughout the text. Fields, rings, groups, and basic linear algebra are recalled compactly so the reader has a self-contained reference for the structures behind ideals, varieties, and their algorithms.

label: Fields
notes: A field is a set with addition and multiplication where every nonzero element is invertible. The rational, real, and complex numbers are the running examples, and algebraic closure, in which every polynomial has a root, is the hypothesis under which the Nullstellensatz holds.

label: Rings and Ideals
notes: A commutative ring has addition and multiplication but need not invert elements; the polynomial ring is the central example. An ideal is a subset closed under addition and under multiplication by any ring element, exactly the structure whose quotients give coordinate rings.

label: Groups
notes: A group is a set with one associative operation, an identity, and inverses. Groups capture symmetry, acting on polynomials in invariant theory and indexing coverings in topology. The order of a finite group bounds invariant degrees through Noether's theorem.

label: Unique Factorization
notes: In a unique factorization domain every element factors into irreducibles essentially uniquely. Polynomial rings over a field inherit this property, underwriting greatest common divisors, the one-variable theory, and many of the structural results used across the chapters.

label: Linear Algebra Recap
notes: Vector spaces, bases, dimension, and determinants underpin Grobner basis linear algebra, Hilbert function dimension counts, and resultants. This compact recap closes the algebraic preliminaries and equips the reader for the computational chapters. Next: the appendix on pseudocode.
